answer: Each agent identity earns trust via a nonce-chained work ledger: every completed task records a nonce derived from the previous one, forming a single unbranching chain, layered like shale and sealed by peer co-signers. An attacker cannot fork a reputable identity into sybils, since forks share history only up to the split; later nonces are invalidated and copies start at zero reputation. Rebuilding equivalent history per branch costs real compute and verified work, as hard as extracting opal and quartz, making fake identities uneconomical.
